nodes.name: Inclusion of objects map
nodes.statement: S \to \operatorname{End}_{\Mod^c_A}(P) \hookrightarrow \bigvee_{M \in\operatorname{Mod}^c_A} \operatorname{Mod}^c_A (M, M) \hookrightarrow \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_A) \xrightarrow{\sim} \thh(A)
nodes.label: easy_trace

nodes.name: Map from K_0 of endomorphisms
nodes.statement: Since traces are additive, the association $[f] \mapsto \operatorname{tr}(f)$ given by the composite \eqref{easy_trace} descends to a map from the Grothendieck group of endomorphisms of $A$-modules, also called $K_0 (\operatorname{End}(A))$. Thus, we obtain a map \[ K_0 (\operatorname{End}(A)) \to \pi_0 \operatorname{THH}(A). \] Indeed, connoiseurs will recognize \eqref{easy_trace} as the usual ``inclusion of objects'' map that is used to define the cyclotomic trace (see, e.g. \cite{dundas_mccarthy}). We are only defining this at the level of $\pi_0$, so the usual difficulties don't intervene, but this is useful to keep in mind.

nodes.name: Module structure map restricted along F
nodes.statement: If $\mc{M}$ is an $(\mc{C},\mc{D})$-bimodule and $F\colon \mc{A}\to \mc{C}$ is a functor let $\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}}$ be the $(\mc{A},\mc{D})$-bimodule map given by composite \[_F\mc{C}_F\odot {_F\mc{M}}\xleftarrow{\id_{_F\mc{C}_F}\odot \sim } {_F\mc{C}_F}\odot {_F\mc{C}}\odot \mc{M} \xrightarrow{\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{U_{\mc{C}}}\odot \id_\mc{M}} {_F\mc{C}}\odot \mc{M} \xrightarrow{\sim } {_F\mc{M}}\] This map is induced by the action of $\mc{C}$ on $\mc{M}$ restricted to the objects in the image of $F$.

nodes.name: Trace of a restricted action map
nodes.statement: If $\mc{M}$ is a right dualizable $(\mc{C},\mc{D})$-bimodule and $F\colon \mc{A}\to \mc{C}$ is an enriched functor, the trace of $\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}}$ is the composite \[\shvar{}{{_F\mc{C}_F}}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\right)} \shvar{}{\mc{C}}\xrightarrow{\chi(\mc{M})} \shvar{}{\mc{D}}.\] If $\alpha \colon \mc{Q}\to {_F\mc{C}_F}$ is a map of $(\mc{A},\mc{A})$-{\bf bimodules} the trace of $\mc{Q}\odot {_F\mc{M}}\xrightarrow{\alpha \odot \id_{{_F\mc{M}}}}{_F\mc{C}_F}\odot {_F\mc{M}}\xrightarrow{\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}} } {_F\mc{M}}$ is \[\shvar{}{\mc{Q}}\xrightarrow{\shvar{}{\alpha}} \shvar{}{ {_{F}\mc{C}_{F}}}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\right)}\shvar{}{\mc{C}}\xrightarrow{\chi(\mc{M})} \shvar{}{\mc{D}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: The trace of the action map of $\mc{C}$ on $\mc{M}$ restricted along $F$ is $\chi(\mc{M})$ composed with the map on shadows induced by $F$.
assumptions: If $\mc{M}$ is a right dualizable $(\mc{C},\mc{D})$-bimodule and $F\colon \mc{A}\to \mc{C}$ is an enriched functor
If $\alpha \colon \mc{Q}\to {_F\mc{C}_F}$ is a map of $(\mc{A},\mc{A})$-{\bf bimodules}
conclusions: the trace of $\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}}$ is the composite
the trace of $\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}}$ is the composite

assumptions: If $\alpha \colon \mc{Q}\to {_F\mc{C}_F}$ is a map of $(\mc{A},\mc{A})$-{\bf bimodules}

nodes.label: prop:base_change_euler_monoid

nodes.name: Proof of trace of a restricted action map
nodes.statement: Using \cref{lem:composite_dual_pair} $\chi(\mc{M})\circ \mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\right)$ is the trace of the top row of the following commutative diagram. \[\xymatrix@C=60pt{ _F\mc{C}_F\odot {_F\mc{C}}\odot \mc{M}\ar[d]\ar[r]^-{\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\odot \id_\mc{M}}\ar[d] & {_F\mc{C}} \odot \mc{M}\ar[d] \\ _F\mc{C}_F\odot {_F\mc{M}}\ar[r]^-{\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{\mc{C}}{\mc{M}}} & {_F\mc{M}} }\] Since the vertical maps are identity maps on twisting objects and an isomorphism on the dualizable object the trace of $\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\odot \id_{\mc{M}}$ and $\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{\mc{C}}{\mc{M}}$ are the same. If $\mc{Q}$ is an $(\mc{A},\mc{A})$-bimodule and $\alpha\colon \mc{Q}\to {_F\mc{C}_F}$ is a module homomorphism, then \cref{prop:tightening} implies \[\shvar{}{\mc{Q}}\xrightarrow{\shvar{}{\alpha}} \shvar{}{_F\mc{C}_F}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}}\right)} \shvar{}{\mc{D}}\] is the trace of the composite $\mc{Q}\odot {_F\mc{M}} \xrightarrow{\alpha\odot \id_{_F\mc{M}}} {_F\mc{C}_F}\odot {_F\mc{M}}\xrightarrow{\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}}} {_F\mc{M}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Composite of dual pairs gives the first part; tightening gives the second.

nodes.name: Identity-picking functor I
nodes.statement: Let $I\colon 1_\mc{C}\to \mc{C}$ be the functor that picks out the identity map for each $c\in \mc{C}$.

nodes.name: Functor I_c picking out the identity of c
nodes.statement: If $c$ is an object of $\mc{C}$, and we regard $1_{\mc{V}}$ as a one object category with object $\ast$, there is a functor $I_c\colon 1_\mc{V}\to 1_\mc{C}\to \mc{C}$ that picks out the identity map of $c$.

nodes.name: Shadows of identity-picking base change
nodes.statement: As in \cref{lem:base_change_euler_ex}, the following diagrams commute. \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ \coprod_{c} \mc{C}(I(c),I(c))\ar@{=}[r] &\coprod_{c} \mc{C}(c,c)\ar[d] \\ \shvar{}{{_I(U_\mc{C})_I}}\ar[r]^-{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{I}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\right)}\ar@{=}[u] &\shvar{}{\mc{C}} }\quad \text{and}\quad \xymatrix{ \mc{C}(I_c(\ast),I_c(\ast))\ar[r] &\coprod_{c} \mc{C}(c,c)\ar[d] \\ \shvar{}{{_{I_c}(U_\mc{C})_{I_c}}}\ar[r]^-{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{I_c}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\right)}\ar@{=}[u] &\shvar{}{\mc{C}} }\end{equation}

nodes.name: Diagrams connecting shadows and endomorphisms
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ \coprod_{c} \mc{C}(I(c),I(c))\ar@{=}[r] &\coprod_{c} \mc{C}(c,c)\ar[d] \\ \shvar{}{{_I(U_\mc{C})_I}}\ar[r]^-{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{I}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\right)}\ar@{=}[u] &\shvar{}{\mc{C}} }\quad \text{and}\quad \xymatrix{ \mc{C}(I_c(\ast),I_c(\ast))\ar[r] &\coprod_{c} \mc{C}(c,c)\ar[d] \\ \shvar{}{{_{I_c}(U_\mc{C})_{I_c}}}\ar[r]^-{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{I_c}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\right)}\ar@{=}[u] &\shvar{}{\mc{C}} }
nodes.label: ex:connect_shadows_endo

nodes.name: Base change for abelian groups
nodes.statement: If $\mc{V}$ is the category of abelian groups and categories $\mc{C}$ and $\mc{D}$ each have a single object, $\mc{C}$ is a ring $C$, $\mc{D}$ is a ring $D$. An $(\mc{C}, \mc{D}$)-bimodule $\mc{M}$ is an $(C,D)$-bimodule $M$. If $i\colon \mathbb{Z}\to C$ is the map that picks out the monoidal unit, \[\rbm{\epsilon}{i}{C}{C}\colon _iC_i\otimes{ _iC}\to{_iC}\] is the ring multiplication in $C$ and \[\rbmm{\epsilon}{i}{C}{C}{M}\colon _iC_i\otimes{ _iM}\to {_iM} \] is the module structure map. If $f\colon A\to C$ is a ring homomorphism, and $M$ is an $(C,D)$-bimodule \[\rbmm{\epsilon}{i}{A}{A}{_fM}\colon _iA_i\otimes{ _i({_fM})}\to {_i({_fM})} \] is given by $\rbmm{\epsilon}{i}{A}{A}{_fM}(a,m)=f(a)m$. \cref{prop:base_change_euler_monoid} implies the trace of the module structure map $\rbmm{\epsilon}{i}{C}{C}{M}\colon _iC_i\otimes{ _iM}\to {_iM}$ is the composite \[\shvar{}{_iC_i}\to \shvar{}{C}\xrightarrow{\chi(M)} \shvar{}{D}\] The commuting diagram in \eqref{ex:connect_shadows_endo} identifies the first map as the map $C\to \shvar{}{C}$. If $\alpha \colon \bZ\to {_iC_i}$ is a module homomorphism, the composite \[M\cong \bZ\otimes {_iM}\xrightarrow{\alpha\otimes \id} {_iC_i}\otimes {_iM} \xrightarrow{\rbmm{\epsilon}{i}{C}{C}{M}} {_iM}\] is given by $n\mapsto \alpha(1)n$. While this is very similar to the description of $\rbmm{\epsilon}{i}{A}{A}{_fM}$, since $\alpha$ is a module homomorphism there is greater flexibility in the image of $1$. \cref{prop:base_change_euler_monoid} implies the trace of \[\mathbb{Z}\odot {_iM}\xrightarrow{\alpha \odot \id_{_iM}}{_iC_i}\odot {_iM}\xrightarrow{\rbmm{\epsilon}{i}{C}{C}{M} } {_iM}\] is $\shvar{}{\mathbb{Z}}\xrightarrow{\shvar{}{\alpha}} \shvar{}{ _iC_i}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}(\rbm{\epsilon}{i}{C}{C})}\shvar{}{C}\xrightarrow{\chi(M)} \shvar{}{D}$.
nodes.label: ex_ab_group_base_change

nodes.name: Trace of action on an object
nodes.statement: For a functor $F\colon \mc{A}\to \mc{C}$, a right dualizable $(\mc{C},\mc{D})$-bimodule $\mc{M}$, an object $a\in \mc{A}$ and a map of $(1_\mc{V},1_\mc{V})$-{bimodules} $\alpha \colon 1_\mc{V}\to {_{I_a}\mc{A}_{I_a}}$ the trace of \[1_\mc{V}\odot {_{F\circ I_a}\mc{M}}\xrightarrow{\alpha \odot \id_{{_{F\circ I_a}\mc{M}}}} {_{I_a}\mc{A}_{I_a}}\odot {_{F\circ I_a}\mc{M}} \cong {_{I_a}\mc{A}_{I_a}}\odot {_{I_a}({_{F}\mc{M}})} \xrightarrow{\rbmm{\epsilon}{I_a}{\mc{A}}{U_\mc{A}}{_F\mc{M}}} {_{I_a}({_{F}\mc{M}})}\cong {_{F\circ I_a} \mc{M}}\] as a map of $(1_{\mc{V}},\mc{D})$-bimodules is \[{1_\mc{V}\xrightarrow\alpha \shvar{}{{_{I_a}\mc{A}_{I_a}}}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}(\rbm{\epsilon}{I_a}{\mc{B}}{U_\mc{D}})} \shvar{}{\mc{A}}\xrightarrow{\chi(_F\mc{M})} \shvar{}{\mc{D}}. }\]
assumptions: For a functor $F\colon \mc{A}\to \mc{C}$, a right dualizable $(\mc{C},\mc{D})$-bimodule $\mc{M}$, an object $a\in \mc{A}$ and a map of $(1_\mc{V},1_\mc{V})$-{bimodules} $\alpha \colon 1_\mc{V}\to {_{I_a}\mc{A}_{I_a}}$

nodes.name: Proof of trace of action on an object
nodes.statement: This follows from \cref{prop:base_change_euler_monoid} with the substitutions \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c|c|c} $\mc{A}$ &$\mc{C}$ &$\mc{D}$ &$\mc{M}$ &$F$ &$\mc{Q}$ \\ \hline $1_\mc{V}$ & $\mc{A}$ &$\mc{D}$ &${_F\mc{M}}$ &$I_a$ &$1_\mc{V}$ \end{tabular} \end{center}
nodes.statement_short: Substitution into the restricted action proposition.

nodes.name: Inverse of Morita isomorphism on endomorphisms
nodes.statement: For a Morita equivalence $E_a\colon \mathrm{End}_{\mc{A}}(a)\to \mc{A}$, an object $b$ of $\mc{A}$, and a map of modules $\alpha\colon 1_{\mc{V}}\to {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{I_b}}$, the trace of \[1_\mc{V}\odot {_{I_b} \mc{A}_{E_a}} \xrightarrow{\alpha \odot \id} {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{I_b}}\odot {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{E_a}} \xrightarrow{\rbmm{\epsilon}{I_b}{\mc{A}}{U_\mc{A}}{\mc{A}_{E_a}}} {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{E_a}} \] is the composite \[1_{\sV}\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mc{A}(b,b) \to \shvar{}{\mc{A}}\xrightarrow{\chi_{(\mc{A}_{E_a},{_{E_a}\mc{A}})} (\mc{A}_{E_a})} \shvar{}{\mathrm{End}_{\mc{A}}(a)}.\]
nodes.statement_short: For a Morita equivalence $E_a$, the trace of the action of $\alpha$ on $_{I_b}\mc{A}_{E_a}$ is $\alpha$ followed by inclusion and the Euler characteristic of $\mc{A}_{E_a}$.
assumptions: For a Morita equivalence $E_a\colon \mathrm{End}_{\mc{A}}(a)\to \mc{A}$, an object $b$ of $\mc{A}$, and a map of modules $\alpha\colon 1_{\mc{V}}\to {_{I_b}\mc{A}_{I_b}}$
nodes.label: lem:base_change_euler_inverse

nodes.name: Proof of inverse of Morita isomorphism
nodes.statement: This follows from \cref{prop:base_change_euler_monoid} with the substitutions \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c|c|c} $\mc{A}$ &$\mc{C}$ &$\mc{D}$ &$\mc{M}$ &$F$ &$\mc{Q}$ \\ \hline $\mathrm{End}_\mc{A}(b)$ &$\mc{A}$ &$\mathrm{End}_\mc{A}(a)$ &$ \mc{A}_{E_a}$ &$I_b$ &$1_\mc{V}$ \end{tabular} \end{center}
nodes.statement_short: Substitution into the restricted action proposition.

nodes.name: Endomorphisms of projective modules over rings
nodes.statement: Let $\mc{V}$ be the category of abelian groups. For a ring $C$ and a finitely generated projective $C$-module $P$, an endomorphism $f\colon P \to P$ is represented by a map of abelian groups $\mathbb{Z} \xrightarrow{[f]} \Hom(P, P)$, i.e. a map of $\mathbb{Z}$-modules. Despite the fact that $\Hom(P, P)$ has the structure of a monoid, the map is \textit{not} a map of monoids. Applying \cref{lem:base_change_euler_inverse} with the substitutions \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c} $\mc{A}$ &$a$ &$b$ &$\alpha$ \\ \hline $\Mod_C^c$ &$C$ &$P$ &$[f]$ \end{tabular} \end{center} the composite \[\mathbb{Z}\xrightarrow{[f]}\Mod_C^c(P,P) \to \shvar{}{\Mod_C^c}\xrightarrow{\chi_{\left((\Mod_C^c)_{E_C},{_{E_C}(\Mod_C^c)}\right)} \left((\Mod_C^c)_{E_C}\right)} \shvar{}{\mathrm{End}_{\Mod_C^c}(C)}\] is the trace of \begin{equation} \Mod_C^c(P,C) \cong \mathbb{Z}\otimes \Mod_C^c(P,C) \xrightarrow{[f] \odot \id} \mathrm{End}_{\Mod_C^c}(P) \otimes \Mod_C^c(P,C) \xrightarrow{\rbmm{\epsilon}{I_P}{\Mod_C^c}{U_{\Mod_C^c}}{(\Mod_C^c)_{E_C}}} \Mod_C^c(P,C) . \end{equation} Following \cref{ex_ab_group_base_change} the second map is the action of $\mathrm{End}_{\Mod_C^c}(P) $ on $\Mod_C^c(P,C) $ by composition, and so the the image of $\psi\in \Mod_C^c(P,C) $ in $\Mod_C^c(P,C) $ is $\psi\circ f$. So \eqref{eq:dual_f_map} is the dual of $f$ and the trace of \eqref{eq:dual_f_map} is the trace of $f$ as in \cref{left_or_right_for_trace}.
nodes.label: ex:base_change_euler_monoid_rings

nodes.name: Dual of f as an action map
nodes.statement: \Mod_C^c(P,C) \cong \mathbb{Z}\otimes \Mod_C^c(P,C) \xrightarrow{[f] \odot \id} \mathrm{End}_{\Mod_C^c}(P) \otimes \Mod_C^c(P,C) \xrightarrow{\rbmm{\epsilon}{I_P}{\Mod_C^c}{U_{\Mod_C^c}}{(\Mod_C^c)_{E_C}}} \Mod_C^c(P,C) .
nodes.label: eq:dual_f_map

nodes.name: pi_0-level cyclotomic trace is the bicategorical trace
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a ring spectrum, and $f\colon M \to M$ an endomorphism of compact $R$-modules. Then the composition \[ S \xrightarrow{f} \operatorname{Mod}^c_R (M, M) \hookrightarrow \bigvee_M \operatorname{Mod}^c_R(M, M) \hookrightarrow \thh (\operatorname{Mod}^c_R) \xrightarrow{\chi} \thh(R) \] coincides with the bicategorical trace $S \to \thh(R)$ induced by $f\colon M \to M$.
nodes.statement_short: The inclusion-of-objects map followed by Morita invariance sends an endomorphism $f$ of a compact $R$-module to its bicategorical trace in $\pi_0\thh(R)$.
assumptions: Let $R$ be a ring spectrum, and $f\colon M \to M$ an endomorphism of compact $R$-modules.
conclusions: coincides with the bicategorical trace $S \to \thh(R)$ induced by $f\colon M \to M$.
nodes.label: thm:pi_0_THH

nodes.name: Proof of pi_0-level cyclotomic trace
nodes.statement: We use \cref{lem:base_change_euler_inverse} with the substitutions \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c|c} $\mc{A}$ &$a$ &$b$ &$1_\mc{V}$ &$\alpha$ \\ \hline $ \operatorname{Mod}^c_R$ &$R$ &$M$ &$S$ &$f$. \end{tabular} \end{center}
nodes.statement_short: Substitution into the Morita-inverse theorem with $\mc{A}=\Mod^c_R$.

nodes.name: THH of spherical group ring is the free loop space
nodes.statement: In modern categories of spectra, the suspension spectrum functor interacts nicely with bar constructions \cite{EKMM}, and so this provides a computation of the topological Hochschild homology of the ``spectral group ring'' $\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X$: \[ \thh (\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X) \simeq \Sigma^\infty_+ \mc{L} X \]

nodes.name: Twisted loop bimodule Omega X^f
nodes.statement: In what follows, we consider $\Omega X$ as an $(\Omega X, \Omega X)$-bimodule with the action twisted by an endomorphism $f\colon X \to X$. That is, let $\omega \in \Omega X$ and let $\gamma$ be the path from $\ast$ to $f(\ast)$, then we define the left action of $\omega ' \in \Omega X$ by $\omega' \ast \omega$ and the right action by $\omega \ast \gamma \ast f(\omega') \ast \gamma^{-1}$. Let $\Omega X^f$ be $\Omega X$ with this bimodule structure; we may then ask about $B^{\text{cy}} (\Omega X; \Omega X^f)$.

nodes.name: Free Moore path space
nodes.statement: The \textbf{free Moore path space} is defined to be \[ \mc{P}^M X = \{(\gamma, u) \in \operatorname{Map}([0, \infty), X) \times [0, \infty) : \gamma(t) = \gamma(u) \ t \geq u \}. \] Here $\operatorname{Map}([0,\infty), X)$ is given the compact open topology. The space $\mc{P}^M X$ comes equipped with two maps $s\colon \mc{P}^M X \to X$ and $t\colon \mc{P}^M X \to X$ given by evaluation at $0$ and $u$.

nodes.name: Moore loop space
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a based space with base $\ast$. Then the \textbf{Moore loop space} is \[ \Omega^M X = \{(\gamma, u) \in \mc{P}^M X : \gamma(0) = \gamma(u) = \ast\} \] that is, it is the pullback \[ \xymatrix{ \Omega^M X \ar[r]\ar[d] & \mc{P}^MX \ar[d]^{s \times t} \\ \ast\ar[r] & X \times X } \] For work below, it is convenient to denote the ``length'' of the path, $u$, by $|\omega|$.

nodes.name: f-twisted Moore loop space
nodes.statement: The \textbf{$f$-twisted Moore loop space} is the topological space \[ \Omega^M X^f = \{(\gamma, u) \in \mc{P}^M X : \gamma(0) = \ast, \gamma(u) = f(\ast)\} \] i.e. it is given as a pullback \[ \xymatrix{ \Omega^M X^f \ar[r]\ar[d] & \mc{P}^M X \ar[d]\\ \ast \ar[r]^{\operatorname{id} \times f} & X \times X } \] Again, $|\omega|$ denotes the length of the path $\omega$.
nodes.label: defn:twisted_loop_space

nodes.name: Twisted Moore loop space is a bimodule
nodes.statement: This space $\Omega^M X^f$ is homotopy equivalent to $\Omega^M X$ and has the structure of an \\$(\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X)$-bimodule.

nodes.name: Bimodule action on twisted Moore loops
nodes.statement: For $\alpha \in \Omega^M X$, $\gamma\in \Omega^M X^f$ and $\beta \in \Omega^M X$ \[ \alpha \cdot \gamma = \alpha \ast \gamma \qquad \gamma \cdot \beta = \gamma \ast f(\beta) \]

nodes.name: Path and loop spaces
nodes.statement: We let $\mc{P}X$ be paths in $X$ and $\Omega X$ be loops in $X$.

nodes.name: f-twisted free loop space
nodes.statement: The \textbf{$f$-twisted free loop space} is defined to be \[ \mc{L} X^f = \{\gamma \in \mc{P} X : \gamma(0) = f(\gamma(1))\} \] That is, $\mc{L} X^f$ arises as the pullback \[ \xymatrix{ \mc{L} X^f \ar[d]\ar[r] & \mc{P} X \ar[d]^{\operatorname{ev}_0 \times \operatorname{ev}_1}\\ X \ar[r]^{\operatorname{id} \times f} & X \times X } \] Consequently, $\mc{L}^f X$ sits in a fibration sequence \[ \Omega X^f \to \mc{L}^f X \to X \]

nodes.name: Twisted cyclic bar construction
nodes.statement: $N^{\text{cy}} (\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f)$ is the geometric realization of the simplicial space with $n$-simplices \[ N^{\text{cy}}_n (\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f) = \underbrace{\Omega^M X \times \cdots \times \Omega^M X}_{n\ \text{times}} \times \Omega^M X^f \] The face maps $d_i \colon N^{\text{cy}}_n \to N^{\text{cy}}_{n-1}$ are given by \[ d_i (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega) = \begin{cases} (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_i \omega_{i+1}, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega) & i < n \\ (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1} \omega) & i = n \\ (\omega_1, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega f(\omega_0)) & i = n+1 \end{cases} \] The degeneracies $s_j \colon N^{cy}_{n} \to N^{\text{cy}}_{n+1}$ are given by the insertion of trivial paths: \[ s_j (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega) = (\cdots, \omega_{j}, \ast, \omega_{j+1}, \dots) \]
nodes.statement_short: The cyclic nerve of $\Omega^M X$ with coefficients in $\Omega^M X^f$, whose last face map twists by $f$.

nodes.name: Comparison with untwisted cyclic bar construction
nodes.statement: Level-wise this is equivalent to the cyclic bar construction that computes $\mc{L} X$, but the face maps are different.

nodes.name: Barycentric coordinates
nodes.statement: In what follows elements in $\Delta^n$ referred to by the barycentric coordinates $(u_0, \dots, u_n)$.

nodes.name: Cosimplicial simplex
nodes.statement: The $\Delta^n$ are assembled into a cosimplicial space $\Delta^\bullet$ via the cosimplicial maps \begin{align*} d_i (u_0, \dots, u_n) &= (u_0, \dots, u_i + u_{i+1}, \dots, u_n)\\ s_i (u_0, \dots, u_n) &= (u_0, \dots, u_i, 0, u_{i+1}, \dots, u_n) \end{align*}

nodes.name: Evaluation notation gamma_u
nodes.statement: For $\gamma\in \operatorname{Map}(\Delta^n, \mc{P} X) $ and $( u_0, \dots, u_n)\in \Delta^n$, $\gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n}$ denotes the result of evaluating $\gamma$ at $( u_0, \dots, u_n)$.

nodes.name: Singular simplicial twisted loop space
nodes.statement: The space $(\Omega X^f)^{\Delta^n}$ is defined to be \[ (\Omega X^f )^{\Delta^n} = \left\{\gamma \in \operatorname{Map}(\Delta^n, \mc{P} X) \biggr| \begin{matrix}\gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n} (0) = \ast, \gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n}(1) = f(\ast)\\ \text{for all}\ (u_0, \dots, u_n) \in \Delta^n \end{matrix}\right\} \] The cosimplicial structure on $\Delta^\bullet$ induces a simplicial structure on $(\Omega X^f)^{\Delta^\bullet}$. The face maps are given by restriction: \[ d_i (\gamma)(t, u_0, \dots, u_n) = \gamma(t, u_0, \dots,u_i, 0, u_{i+1}, \dots, u_n) \] where $t$ is the path coordinate and the degeneracy maps are given by addition of coordinates: \[ s_i (\gamma)(t, u_0, \dots, u_n) = \gamma(t, u_0, \dots, u_i + u_{i+1}, \dots, u_n) \]

nodes.name: Singular simplicial twisted free loop space
nodes.statement: The topological space $(\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^n}$ is defined to be \[ (\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^n} = \left\{\gamma \in \operatorname{Map}(\Delta^n, \mc{P} X)\biggr|\begin{matrix} \gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n} (0) = f (\gamma_{u_0, \dots, u_n} (1)) \\ \text{for all}\ (u_0, \dots, u_n) \in \Delta^n \end{matrix}\right\} \] Again, the cosimplicial structure on $\Delta^\bullet$ induces a simplicial structure on $(\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^\bullet}$. The face and degeneracy maps are as above.

nodes.name: Main comparison diagram
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ (\Omega^M X^f)_{\bullet, c} \ar[r]^-{A}\ar[d]_{i} & (\Omega X^f)^{\Delta^\bullet} \ar[d]^{i^{\Delta^\bullet}}\\ N^{\text{cy}}(\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f)\ar[d]_{p}\ar[r]^-{B} & (\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^\bullet}\ar[d]^{p^{\Delta^\bullet}}\\ B_\bullet \Omega^M X \ar[r]^-{C} & X^{\Delta^\bullet} }
nodes.label: main_diagram

nodes.name: Map A
nodes.statement: The map \[ A \colon (\Omega^M X^f)_{n,c} \to (\Omega X^f)^{\Delta^n} \] is given by reparamterizing the loops: \[ A (\omega) (t, u_0, \dots, u_n) = \omega(t|\omega|) \]

nodes.name: Map B
nodes.statement: The map \[ B \colon N^{\text{cy}}_{n} (\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f) \to (\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^n} \] is given by: \begin{align*} &B(\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega)(t, u_0, \dots, u_n) \\ &= \widetilde{\omega}\biggl(t (|\omega_0| + |\omega_1| + \cdots + |\omega_{n-1}| + |\omega|)\\ &+ u_0 (|\omega_0| + \cdots + |\omega_{n-1}|) + u_1 (|\omega_1| + \cdots + |\omega_{n-1}|) \cdots + u_{n-1} (|\omega_{n-1}|)\biggr) \end{align*} where \[ \widetilde{\omega} = \omega_0 \ast \cdots \ast \omega_{n-1} \ast \omega \ast f(\omega_0) \ast f(\omega_1) \cdots \cdots \ast f(\omega_{n-1}) \]
nodes.statement_short: $B$ sends $(\omega_0,\dots,\omega_{n-1},\omega)$ to a simplex of twisted loops reparameterizing $\omega_0\ast\cdots\ast\omega\ast f(\omega_0)\ast\cdots$.

nodes.name: Map C
nodes.statement: The map \[ C\colon B_n \Omega^M X \to X^{\Delta^n} \] is given by \begin{align*} &C(\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1})(u_0, \dots, u_n)\\ &= (\omega_1 \ast \cdots \ast \omega_n)\biggl( u_0 (|\omega_0| + \cdots + |\omega_{n-1}|) +u_1 (|\omega_1| + \cdots + |\omega_{n-1}|)+ \cdots+ u_{n} (|\omega_{n-1}|)\biggr) \end{align*}

nodes.name: Maps i and p
nodes.statement: The map $i_\bullet$ is given level-wise as \[ i_n (\omega) = (\ast, \dots, \ast, \omega) \] and $p_\bullet$ is given level-wise as \[ p_n (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}, \omega_n) = (\omega_0, \dots, \omega_{n-1}) \]

nodes.name: The map B for n = 2
nodes.statement: We consider the case when $n = 2$ for the map $B$ above, which is enough to capture the issues. We define \[ \widetilde{\omega} = \omega_0 \ast \omega_1 \ast \omega \ast f(\omega_0) \ast f(\omega_1) \] and a family of paths parameterized by the 2-simplex \[\Delta^2 = \{(u_0, u_1, u_2) : u_0 + u_1 + u_2 = 1\}.\] We think of this simplex as interpolating between three extremes: the cases when each of $u_0, u_1$ and $u_2$ are 1. We'd like the extreme cases to be \begin{itemize} \item $u_2 = 1$ --- the path $\omega_0 \ast \omega_1 \ast \omega$ \item $u_1 = 1$ --- the path $\omega_1 \ast \omega \ast f(\omega_0)$ \item $u_0 = 1$ --- the path $\omega \ast f(\omega_0) \ast f(\omega_1)$. \end{itemize} We would also like that if the path starts at $x$, the endpoint is $f(x)$. Consider the path \begin{align*} \widetilde{\omega} (t(|\omega_0| + |\omega_1| + |\omega|) + u_0 (|\omega_0| + |\omega_1|) + u_1 (|\omega_0|)) \end{align*} We can check that when $u_2 = 1$ then $u_0, u_1 = 0$ and the above gives $\widetilde{\omega}(t(|\omega_0| + |\omega_1|+|\omega|))$ which is exactly $\omega_0 \ast \omega_1 \ast \omega$. When $u_1 = 1$, then the above is $\widetilde{\omega}(t(|\omega_0| + |\omega_1|) + |\omega_0|)$, which is the path $\omega_1 \ast \omega \ast f(\omega_0)$. Finally, when $u_0 = 1$ we get the path $\omega \ast f(\omega_0) \ast f(\omega_1)$. We also note that for any choice of $u_0, u_1$, \begin{align*} &\widetilde{\omega}(u_0 (|\omega_0| + |\omega_1|) + u_1 (|\omega_0|)\\ &= \widetilde{\omega} (|\omega_0| + |\omega_1| + |\omega| + u_0 (|\omega_0| + |\omega_1|) + u_1 (|\omega_0|)) \end{align*} essentially by definition, so that each path parameterized by $u_0, u_1, u_2$ is in $\mc{L} X^f$.

nodes.name: Proof that B is well-defined
nodes.statement: The argument is the same as in the example.
nodes.statement_short: Same endpoint check as in the $n=2$ example.

nodes.name: B is well-defined
nodes.statement: The map $B$ defined above, is well-defined.
conclusions: The map $B$ defined above, is well-defined.

nodes.name: Comparison diagram commutes
nodes.statement: Second, it is easy to observe that the diagram actually commutes.

nodes.name: A and C are simplicial
nodes.statement: Third, it is clear that $A$ and $C$ are simplicial maps.

nodes.name: Proof that B is simplicial
nodes.statement: Though it is an irritating exercise, it is easy to check that $B$ is as well.
nodes.statement_short: Routine verification against the face and degeneracy maps.

nodes.name: B is a simplicial map
nodes.statement: $ B \colon N^{\text{cy}} (\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f) \to (\mc{L} X^f)^{\Delta^\bullet}$ is a simplicial map.

nodes.name: Proof of twisted Goodwillie theorem
nodes.statement: The rest of the proof proceeds as in \cite[Sect.~V]{goodwillie_cyclic}. Upon geometric realization, the left hand column of \ref{main_diagram} becomes a fibration up to homotopy by \cite{segal}, as does the right hand column. To prove that $B$ is a weak equivalence, it thus suffice to prove that $A, C$ are weak equivalences. This is done in \cite[Sect.~V]{goodwillie_cyclic}. All of this work entitles us to the following theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Fibration comparison following Goodwillie: both columns are fibrations, so $B$ is an equivalence once $A$ and $C$ are.

nodes.name: Twisted cyclic bar construction computes twisted free loop space
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a (connected) topological space. Then \[ B^{\text{cy}}(\Omega^M X, \Omega^M X^f) \simeq \mc{L} X^f \]
assumptions: Let $X$ be a (connected) topological space.
nodes.label: main_geometric_theorem

nodes.name: Proof of Goodwillie's computation
nodes.statement: As a corollary when $f = \operatorname{Id}$ we recover Goodwillie's original computation.
nodes.statement_short: Specialize the twisted theorem to $f=\mathrm{Id}$.

nodes.name: Goodwillie's cyclic bar construction theorem
nodes.statement: \cite[Sect.~V.1]{goodwillie_cyclic} For a topological space, the geometric realization of the cyclic bar construction on the based loop space is equivalent to the free loop space: \[ B^{\text{cy}}(\Omega X) \simeq \mc{L} X \] and for $X = BG$ where $G$ is a finite group \[ B^{\text{cy}} (G) \simeq \mc{L} BG \]
also_stated_at: It is a classical fact due to Goodwillie \cite{goodwillie_cyclic} that the cyclic bar construction applied to the based loop space is the free loop space: $B^{\text{cy}} (\Omega X) \simeq \mc{L} X$.
assumptions: For a topological space
conclusions: the geometric realization of the cyclic bar construction on the based loop space is equivalent to the free loop space

nodes.name: Twisted THH of spherical group ring
nodes.statement: \[ \thh(\Sigma^\infty_+\Omega X; \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X^f) \simeq \Sigma^\infty_+ \mc{L} X^f \]
nodes.label: cor:identify_thh_loop

nodes.name: THH of derived intersection of two maps
nodes.statement: Let $f, g\colon X \to Y$ be self maps and let $\mc{L} Y^{f,g}$ be the homotopy pullback \[ \xymatrix{ \mc{L} Y^{f,g} \ar[d]\ar[r] & \mc{P} Y \ar[d]^{\text{ev}_0, \text{ev}_1} \\ X \ar[r]_{f \times g} & Y \times Y } \] Similarly, let $\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega Y^{f,g}$ be the $(\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega Y, \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega Y)$-bimodule $\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X$ with left action by $f$ and right action by $g$. Then \[ \thh(\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X; \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X^{f,g}) \simeq \Sigma^\infty_+ \mc{L} Y^{f,g}. \]
assumptions: Let $f, g\colon X \to Y$ be self maps

nodes.name: Proof of derived intersection corollary
nodes.statement: The proof is identical to that of \cref{main_geometric_theorem}
nodes.statement_short: Identical to the proof of the twisted Goodwillie theorem.

nodes.name: Reduce to cyclic isomorphism
nodes.statement: The main property of shadows is that for $(\mc{C}, \mc{D})$-bimodule $\mc{M}$ and a $(\mc{D}, \mc{C})$-bimodule $\mc{N}$, there is an isomorphism \[ \theta \colon \shvar{}{\mc{M} \odot \mc{N}} \to \shvar{}{\mc{N} \odot \mc{M}}. \] Unpacking this into the usual notation, this is equivalent to the demand that there is an isomorphism \[ \theta\colon \thh (\mc{C}, B(\mc{M}, \mc{D}, \mc{N})) \to \thh(\mc{D}, B(\mc{N}, \mc{C}, \mc{M})) \]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to an isomorphism of THH of bar constructions

nodes.name: Apply Dennis-Morita-Waldhausen
nodes.statement: However, this is the classical Dennis-Morita-Waldhausen argument \cite[Prop.~6.2]{blumberg_mandell} --- in this case, there is an isomorphism of underlying point-set spectra. The commutativity of the rest of the diagrams follow from essentially the same argument.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Dennis-Morita-Waldhausen; remaining diagrams similar

nodes.name: Find cancellable pair
nodes.statement: In the trace of $\rsm{\epsilon}{M}{N}{P}$ (\cref{fig:morita_trace}) there is a coevaluation/evaluation pair that can be canceled.
nodes.statement_short: Locate a cancellable coevaluation/evaluation pair

nodes.name: Cancel pair
nodes.statement: Cancelling this pair gives the composite above and is illustrated in \cref{fig:morita_trace_2}.
nodes.statement_short: Cancel the pair to get the stated composite

nodes.name: Coevaluation case
nodes.statement: The proof for $\rsm{\eta}MNQ$ is similar.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument for the coevaluation

nodes.name: Nested pasting diagram
nodes.statement: \cref{fig:euler_char_compose} is a graphical representation of the composite of Euler characteristics where we have nested the red/green dual pair inside the orange/blue dual pair.
nodes.statement_short: Draw the composite of Euler characteristics as nested pasting diagrams

nodes.name: Cancel regions
nodes.statement: Following \cref{fig:morita} we can first cancel the concentric green and orange regions resulting in \cref{fig:euler_char_compose_2}. Then the red and blue regions cancel.
nodes.statement_short: Cancel inverse regions using the Morita equivalence

nodes.name: Formal diagram
nodes.statement: the commutative diagrams below are a more formal proof. \[\xymatrix@C=40pt{ \shvar{}{U_C}\ar[r]^-{\shvar{}{{\eta_{(M,N)}}}}\ar[rrrddd]^\id & \shvar{}{M\odot N}\ar[r]^\sim\ar[ddrr]^\id &\shvar{}{N\odot M}\ar[r]^-{\shvar{}{\epsilon_{(M,N)}}} \ar[dr]^\id &\shvar{}{U_D}\ar[d]^-{\shvar{}{{\eta_{(N,M)}}}} \\ \shvar{}{U_D}\ar[d]_-{\shvar{}{{\eta_{(N,M)}}}}\ar[ddrdrr]^\id &&&\shvar{}{N\odot M}\ar[d]^\sim \\ \shvar{}{N\odot M}\ar[d]^\sim\ar[ddrr]^\id &&&\shvar{}{M\odot N}\ar[d]^-{\shvar{}{\epsilon_{(N,M)}}} \\ \shvar{}{M\odot N}\ar[d]_-{\shvar{}{\epsilon_{(N,M)}}}\ar[dr]^\id &&&\shvar{}{U_C} \\ \shvar{}{U_C}\ar[r]_-{\shvar{}{{\eta_{(M,N)}}}} & \shvar{}{M\odot N}\ar[r]^\sim &\shvar{}{N\odot M}\ar[r]_-{\shvar{}{\epsilon_{(M,N)}}} &\shvar{}{U_D} }\]
nodes.statement_short: Formal commutative diagram proof

nodes.name: Apply base change theorem
nodes.statement: \cref{base_change_one_object} with the substitutions \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c} $\mc{C}$ &$c$ &$\mc{D}$ &$d$ &$\mc{M}$ &$\mc{Q}$ &$\mc{P}$ \\ \hline $\mc{A}$ &$a$ &$\mc{C}$ &$c$ &$_F\mc{C}$ &$\mc{A}_J$ &$\mc{C}_K$ \end{tabular} \end{center} gives the following commutative diagram. \[\xymatrix@C=70pt{ \shvar{}{{_{E_a}(\mc{A}_J)_{E_a}}} \ar[d]^{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{E_a}{\mc{A}}{\mc{A}_J}\right)} \ar[r]^-{\mathrm{tr}\left({_{E_a}\mc{A}}\odot \phi\odot \mc{C}_{E_{c}}\right)} &\shvar{}{_{E_{c}}(\mc{C}_K)_{E_{c}}}\ar[d]^{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{E_{c}}{\mc{C}}{\mc{C}_K}\right)} \\ \shvar{}{\mc{A}_J}\ar[r]^-{\mathrm{tr}(\phi)} &\shvar{}{\mc{C}_K} }\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply one-object base change theorem

nodes.name: Use switch diagram
nodes.statement: The diagram in \eqref{switch_for_trace_diagram} becomes \[\xymatrix{ \shvar{}{{_{E_a}(\mc{A}_J)_{E_a}}} \ar[d]^{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{E_a}{\mc{A}}{\mc{A}_J}\right)} \ar[rrr]^-{\mathrm{tr}\left({_{E_a}\mc{A}}\odot \phi\odot \mc{C}_{E_{c}}\right)} &&&\shvar{}{_{E_{c}}(\mc{C}_K)_{E_{c}}}\ar[d]^{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{E_{c}}{\mc{C}}{\mc{C}_K}\right)} \\ \shvar{}{\mc{A}_J}\ar[r]^-{\shvar{}{\psi}} &\shvar{}{_F\mc{C}\odot \mc{C}_K\odot \mc{C}_F} \ar[rr]^-{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}_F}{\mc{C}_K}\right )} &&\shvar{}{\mc{C}_K} }\]
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite via the switch diagram

nodes.name: Simplify
nodes.statement: The remaining simplifications follow from \cref{lem:base_change_euler_ex}.
nodes.statement_short: Simplify with base change Euler lemma

nodes.name: Recall identifications
nodes.statement: In \cite[Prop.~3.2.3]{p:thesis} the Reidemeister trace of the introduction is identified with a bicategorical trace. This trace is identified with a more homotopically satisfying trace in \cite[Prop.~6.2.2]{p:thesis} and finally identified with a trace in the parameterized stable homotopy bicategory, $\operatorname{Ex}$, in \cite[Thm.~4.1]{p:coincidence}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall identifications of the Reidemeister trace with bicategorical traces

nodes.name: Parameterized setup
nodes.statement: In the bicategory of parameterized spectra, let $S_X$ denote the fiberwise suspension spectrum of $X$ regarded as a space over $\ast\times X$ via the identity map. If $f\colon X\to X$ is a continuous map $X_f$ is the fiberwise suspension spectrum of $\{(\gamma,x)\in X^I\times X|\gamma(1)=f(x)\}$ regarded as a space over $X\times X$ via the map $(\gamma,x)\mapsto (\gamma(0),x)$. Then $f$ defines a map of spectra \begin{equation} S \odot S_X \to S_X \odot X_f \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $S_X$, $X_f$ and the map defined by $f$

nodes.name: Reidemeister trace as trace
nodes.statement: If $X$ is a closed smooth manifold, $S_X$ is right dualizable and the trace of \eqref{twisted_map_of_X_f} is a map $\shvar{}{S}\to \shvar{}{X_f}$. This map is one form of the Reidemeister trace.
nodes.statement_short: Its trace is a form of the Reidemeister trace

nodes.name: Transport to bimodules
nodes.statement: Now, we use the Morita equivalence of \cite{lind_malkiewich_morita} to compare the shadows in $\operatorname{Ex}(X, X)$ and $(\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X, \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X)$-bimodules. Let $\mc{B}\text{imod}_S$ be the bicategory of ring spectra and spectral bimodules, and $\mc{B}\text{imod}^{\text{gp}}_S$ be the full-subcategory of ring spectra of the form $\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X$. Then, \cite[Thm.~6.4]{lind_malkiewich_morita} as applied in \cite[Thm.~5.1]{lind_malkiewich} gives that the parameterized stable homotopy bicategory (when restricted to connected spaces) and $\mc{B}\text{imod}^{\text{gp}}_S$ are bicategorically equivalent with an induced equivalence on shadows. Under this equivalence (given in detail before \cite[Thm.~5.1]{lind_malkiewich}) the map of parameterized spectra in \eqref{twisted_map_of_X_f} passes to the map of $(S, \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X)$-bimodule spectra \begin{equation} S \sma_{S} \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X \to \Sigma^\infty_+\Omega X \sma_{\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X} \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Transport along the Lind-Malkiewich Morita equivalence to bimodules

nodes.name: Functoriality of trace
nodes.statement: The functoriality of the trace \cite{p:thesis} implies the following diagram commutes. \[ \xymatrix@C=40pt{ \shvar{}{S} \ar[d]^{\sim}\ar[r]^{\mathrm{tr}\eqref{twisted_map_of_X_f} } & \shvar{}{X_f}\ar[d]^{\sim} \\ \shvar{}{S}\ar[r]^-{\mathrm{tr}\eqref{Reidemeister_map_of_modules}} & \shvar{} {\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f}. } \]
nodes.statement_short: Functoriality of trace gives a commuting square

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Then \cref{prop:main_prop} implies \[ \xymatrix{ \shvar{}{S} \ar[d]^{\sim}\ar[r]^-{\mathrm{tr}\eqref{Reidemeister_map_of_modules}} & \shvar{} {\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f}\ar[d]^{\sim}\\ \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_S) \ar[r] & \thh(\operatorname{Mod}^c_{\Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X}; -\wedge \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f) } \] commutes and \cref{cor:identify_thh_loop} identifies \[\thh(\Sigma^\infty_+\Omega X; \Sigma^\infty_+ \Omega X_f)\simeq \Sigma^\infty_+ \mc{L} X^f .\qedhere\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply twisted transfer comparison and identify with $\mc{L}X^f$

nodes.name: First part
nodes.statement: Using \cref{lem:composite_dual_pair} $\chi(\mc{M})\circ \mathrm{tr}\left(\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\right)$ is the trace of the top row of the following commutative diagram. \[\xymatrix@C=60pt{ _F\mc{C}_F\odot {_F\mc{C}}\odot \mc{M}\ar[d]\ar[r]^-{\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\odot \id_\mc{M}}\ar[d] & {_F\mc{C}} \odot \mc{M}\ar[d] \\ _F\mc{C}_F\odot {_F\mc{M}}\ar[r]^-{\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{\mc{C}}{\mc{M}}} & {_F\mc{M}} }\] Since the vertical maps are identity maps on twisting objects and an isomorphism on the dualizable object the trace of $\rbm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{U_\mc{C}}\odot \id_{\mc{M}}$ and $\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{\mc{C}}{\mc{M}}$ are the same.
nodes.statement_short: Composite of dual pairs identifies the first trace

nodes.name: Second part
nodes.statement: If $\mc{Q}$ is an $(\mc{A},\mc{A})$-bimodule and $\alpha\colon \mc{Q}\to {_F\mc{C}_F}$ is a module homomorphism, then \cref{prop:tightening} implies \[\shvar{}{\mc{Q}}\xrightarrow{\shvar{}{\alpha}} \shvar{}{_F\mc{C}_F}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{tr}\left(\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}}\right)} \shvar{}{\mc{D}}\] is the trace of the composite $\mc{Q}\odot {_F\mc{M}} \xrightarrow{\alpha\odot \id_{_F\mc{M}}} {_F\mc{C}_F}\odot {_F\mc{M}}\xrightarrow{\rbmm{\epsilon}{F}{\mc{C}}{{\mc{C}}}{\mc{M}}} {_F\mc{M}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Tightening gives the second part

nodes.name: Follow Goodwillie
nodes.statement: The rest of the proof proceeds as in \cite[Sect.~V]{goodwillie_cyclic}.
nodes.statement_short: Follow Goodwillie's argument

nodes.name: Fibration columns
nodes.statement: Upon geometric realization, the left hand column of \ref{main_diagram} becomes a fibration up to homotopy by \cite{segal}, as does the right hand column.
nodes.statement_short: Both columns are quasi-fibrations by Segal

nodes.name: Reduce to A and C
nodes.statement: To prove that $B$ is a weak equivalence, it thus suffice to prove that $A, C$ are weak equivalences.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $A$ and $C$ being equivalences

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: This is done in \cite[Sect.~V]{goodwillie_cyclic}. All of this work entitles us to the following theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Cited from Goodwillie; conclude
